rationale: Carcinoma ex pleomorphic adenoma is a salivary gland malignancy that arises wherever pleomorphic adenoma/salivary tissue occurs (major and minor glands across the head and neck), matching the code's salivary-bearing ceiling; it is not restricted to a proper subset.
source_name: Head and Neck Pathology - Carcinoma Ex Pleomorphic Adenoma (WHO)

rationale: A carcinosarcoma arising ex pleomorphic adenoma is a salivary malignant mixed tumor occurring across major and minor salivary sites of the head/neck represented in the ceiling; no proper-subset restriction is established.
source_name: Head and Neck Pathology - Carcinoma Ex Pleomorphic Adenoma (WHO)

rationale: Epithelial-myoepithelial carcinoma ex PA is one of the histologic subtypes of carcinoma ex pleomorphic adenoma and occurs across the salivary-gland distribution covered by the code ceiling; not restricted to a subset.
source_name: Head and Neck Pathology - Carcinoma Ex Pleomorphic Adenoma (WHO)

rationale: Mucoepidermoid carcinoma ex PA is a recognized luminal-differentiation subtype of carcinoma ex pleomorphic adenoma arising across major/minor salivary sites in the ceiling; not restricted to a proper subset.
source_name: Head and Neck Pathology - Carcinoma Ex Pleomorphic Adenoma (WHO)

rationale: Myoepithelial carcinoma ex PA is a non-luminal subtype of carcinoma ex pleomorphic adenoma occurring across the salivary distribution of the code ceiling; no anatomic proper-subset restriction is documented.
source_name: Head and Neck Pathology - Carcinoma Ex Pleomorphic Adenoma (WHO)

term: Salivary duct carcinoma ex pleomorphic adenoma
rationale: Salivary duct carcinoma ex PA is the most common luminal subtype of carcinoma ex pleomorphic adenoma; it arises in major (esp. parotid) and minor salivary glands across the head/neck sites in the ceiling, not a proper subset.
source_name: PubMed PMID25579019 - Salivary duct carcinoma ex PA of the palate (minor and major glands)

rationale: The term specifically names the salivary gland; salivary carcinosarcoma (true malignant mixed tumor) is a salivary gland neoplasm and does not occur at the many non-salivary sites (esophagus, stomach, colon, lung, uterus, thyroid, etc.) included in this code's broad ceiling, so it is restricted to the salivary-bearing head/neck subset.
source_name: Dentomaxillofacial Radiology / WHO salivary gland tumours - carcinosarcoma (true malignant mixed tumor) of salivary gland

rationale: Carcinosarcoma, NOS is a generic biphasic malignancy descriptor applied across many organ systems (the code ceiling spans GI, GU, lung, uterus, head/neck, etc.); it is not anatomically restricted.
source_name: StatPearls / general - carcinosarcoma NOS is a multi-site descriptor

rationale: Ameloblastic carcinoma arises predominantly intraosseously in the jaws but well-documented peripheral (gingival/extraosseous) variants exist, so it spans both the gingival mucosa and jawbone codes of the ceiling; not a proper subset.
source_name: StatPearls - Odontogenic Tumors of the Jaws (WHO classification)

rationale: 'Central intraosseous' by definition denotes a carcinoma arising within the jawbone (mandible/maxilla) with no connection to the surface mucosa, excluding the gingival mucosal codes of the ceiling.
source_name: PMC - Primary intraosseous carcinoma; central intraosseous mucoepidermoid carcinoma of the jawbone

rationale: A central intraosseous mucoepidermoid tumor arises within the mandible/maxilla bone by definition (central = intraosseous), so it is restricted to the jawbone codes rather than the gingival mucosa.
source_name: PMC - central intraosseous mucoepidermoid carcinoma of the jawbone

rationale: Odontogenic carcinoma is a generic category of malignant odontogenic tumors of the tooth-bearing jaw region, encompassing both intraosseous and gingival/peripheral lesions; it is not restricted to a proper subset of the small jaw ceiling.
source_name: StatPearls - Odontogenic Tumors of the Jaws (WHO classification)

rationale: Odontogenic sarcoma (e.g., ameloblastic fibrosarcoma) is a malignant odontogenic tumor of the jaw region; as a generic entity it is not clearly restricted to bone-only versus gingival codes within the small jaw ceiling.
source_name: StatPearls - Odontogenic Tumors of the Jaws (WHO classification)

rationale: 'Odontogenic tumor, malignant' is a generic descriptor for malignant tumors of the odontogenic (tooth-bearing jaw) apparatus and is not restricted to a proper subset of the jaw ceiling.
source_name: StatPearls - Odontogenic Tumors of the Jaws (WHO classification)

rationale: Primary intraosseous carcinoma (PIOC) is defined by WHO as a carcinoma arising WITHIN the jawbone with no initial connection to the oral mucosa; it therefore involves the mandible/maxilla bone, not the gingival mucosal codes.
source_name: PMC - Primary intraosseous carcinoma of the mandible (WHO definition: within jawbone, no mucosal connection)

rationale: PIOSCC is defined by WHO as a central jaw squamous cell carcinoma arising within the jawbone from odontogenic epithelial remnants, with no initial connection to the oral mucosa; restricted to mandible/maxilla bone.
source_name: Annali di Stomatologia / WHO - Primary intraosseous squamous cell carcinoma arising within the jawbones

rationale: WHO 5th ed defines sclerosing odontogenic carcinoma as a rare PRIMARY INTRAOSSEOUS carcinoma of the jaws (mandible > maxilla); it arises within jawbone, excluding the gingival mucosal codes.
source_name: Head and Neck Pathology / WHO - Sclerosing odontogenic carcinoma is a primary intraosseous carcinoma of the jaws

rationale: Ghost cell odontogenic carcinoma is characterized as an intraosseous malignant odontogenic tumor of the maxilla/mandible bone; despite exceedingly rare peripheral reports it is defined by intraosseous (central) location, restricting it to the jawbone codes.
source_name: PMC - Ghost cell odontogenic carcinoma characterized by intra-osseous location (maxilla/mandible)

rationale: Clear cell odontogenic carcinoma is consistently described as a rare INTRAOSSEOUS carcinoma of the jaw, arising centrally within the mandible (predominantly) or maxilla; restricted to the jawbone codes, not gingival mucosa.
source_name: World Journal of Surgical Oncology - Clear cell odontogenic carcinoma is a rare intraosseous carcinoma of the jaw

rationale: Clear cell odontogenic tumor (synonym of clear cell odontogenic carcinoma) is a rare intraosseous jaw neoplasm arising centrally within the mandible/maxilla bone; restricted to the jawbone codes.
source_name: World Journal of Surgical Oncology - clear cell odontogenic carcinoma/tumor, intraosseous jaw

rationale: Odontogenic carcinosarcoma is an exceedingly rare malignant odontogenic tumor of the jaw region; as a distinct but broadly-defined odontogenic entity it is not established as restricted to a proper subset of the small jaw ceiling.
source_name: StatPearls - Odontogenic Tumors of the Jaws (WHO classification)

term: Melanotic neuroectodermal tumor of infancy, malignant
rationale: MNTI is a craniofacial neural-crest tumor that predominates in the maxilla/anterior alveolus but also arises in the oral cavity, gingiva, palate, mandible and nasal region represented in the ceiling; it is not confined to a single clean anatomic subset of these craniofacial mucosal sites.
source_name: StatPearls - Melanotic Neuroectodermal Tumor of Infancy

rationale: Melanotic neuroectodermal tumor, malignant occurs across the craniofacial mucosal/nasal sites (maxilla-predominant but also palate, gingiva, oral cavity, nasal) that make up the code ceiling; no proper-subset restriction is established.
source_name: StatPearls - Melanotic Neuroectodermal Tumor of Infancy

rationale: Alveolar soft part sarcoma is a soft-tissue sarcoma arising in deep soft tissues (including head/neck sites such as tongue and orbit in children and extremity/trunk soft tissue in adults) matching the soft-tissue sites of the ceiling; it is not restricted to a proper subset.
source_name: General pathology reference - alveolar soft part sarcoma is a broadly-distributed soft-tissue sarcoma
